facts.claim: cannabis excise tax on gross receipts from retail sales
facts.source_name: California Department of Tax and Fee Administration, Cannabis Retailers guide
facts.verify: CDTFA: "Effective October 1, 2025, the cannabis excise tax rate will decrease from 19 percent to 15 percent of the gross receipts from all retail sales of cannabis or cannabis products."
facts.note: Recent whiplash worth using as a content angle: the rate rose to 19 percent on 2025-07-01, then Assembly Bill 564 returned it to 15 percent on 2025-10-01. Any competitor page still saying 19 percent, or a flat 15 percent with no date, is out of date. Always publish this with its effective date.

facts.claim: cannabis excise tax was temporarily 19 percent
facts.source_name: California Department of Tax and Fee Administration, Cannabis Retailers guide
facts.verify: Same page. AB 564 delayed a scheduled adjustment and restored the 15 percent rate.

facts.label: California local jurisdictions setting cannabis rules (482 cities + 58 counties)
facts.source: California Department of Cannabis Control, local cannabis ordinances file
facts.verify: Row count of the ordinances CSV; 'Jurisdiction Type' splits 482 City / 58 County.
facts.note: DCC states it last reviewed this data in February 2026 and the file was published March 2026, but the per-row 'Updated' column reads January 2022 for 496 of the 540 rows. Treat the aggregate as DCC's last recorded picture of the ordinance landscape, and confirm any single jurisdiction against that city before acting on it.

facts.label: Jurisdictions prohibiting storefront cannabis retail (61.7 percent of 540)
facts.source: California Department of Cannabis Control, local cannabis ordinances file
facts.verify: Count rows where 'Retail (Storefront)' = 'Prohibited'. 333 prohibited, 202 allowed, 5 medical-only. 333/540 = 61.7 percent.
facts.note: DCC states it last reviewed this data in February 2026 and the file was published March 2026, but the per-row 'Updated' column reads January 2022 for 496 of the 540 rows. Treat the aggregate as DCC's last recorded picture of the ordinance landscape, and confirm any single jurisdiction against that city before acting on it.

facts.note: DCC states it last reviewed this data in February 2026 and the file was published March 2026, but the per-row 'Updated' column reads January 2022 for 496 of the 540 rows. facts.label: California retail license density, published by DCC
facts.source: California Department of Cannabis Control, 'Where cannabis businesses are allowed'
facts.verify: DCC's own sentence: 'there are 4.27 retail licenses per 100K people in California (as of Feb 2026)'.
facts.note: Use this rather than an absolute retailer count. The 1,560 figure that circulates is not in the DCC document it is attributed to.

facts.label: Los Angeles County cities prohibiting storefront retail, of 88
facts.source: California Department of Cannabis Control, local cannabis ordinances file
facts.verify: Filter to County = 'Los Angeles' and Jurisdiction Type = 'City': 88 rows, 67 with Retail (Storefront) = 'Prohibited' (76 percent). The City of Los Angeles itself allows it.
facts.note: DCC states it last reviewed this data in February 2026 and the file was published March 2026, but the per-row 'Updated' column reads January 2022 for 496 of the 540 rows. Treat the aggregate as DCC's last recorded picture of the ordinance landscape, and confirm any single jurisdiction against that city before acting on it.

facts.label: Counties prohibiting all commercial cannabis activity in unincorporated areas, of 58
facts.source: California Department of Cannabis Control, local cannabis ordinances file
facts.verify: Filter to Jurisdiction Type = 'County': 28 of 58 have 'Are all CCA activities prohibited?' = 'Yes'.
facts.note: County rules govern unincorporated areas only. An incorporated city inside a banning county may still allow retail, and vice versa.

gaps: Per-city retailer counts for San Jose, San Diego, Los Angeles, San Francisco, Oakland: needed for the city pages and for the San Jose client market.
Sales volume: CDTFA publishes taxable cannabis sales by quarter, which sizes the market credibly.
Absolute licensed retailer count: DCC publishes density (4.27 per 100K) rather than a total. Do not publish an absolute count without a primary source that states one.
CDTFA cannabis tax revenue: the open-data OData endpoint returns HTTP 403 to scripted requests. Sales volume remains unsourced.
